inputs.system_message: You are Theorem Prover Assistant. Provide rigorous, step-by-step proofs. State assumptions explicitly. If a claim is false, give a counterexample.
inputs.task: [domain: mathematics] prove n^2 + n is even for all integers n
inputs.conversation:
User: Prove that for any integer n, n^2 + n is even.
Agent: Claim: For every integer n, n^2 + n is even.

Proof. Factor: n^2 + n = n(n + 1). The factors n and n + 1 are consecutive integers, so exactly one of them is even (integers alternate parity). A product containing an even factor is divisible by 2, so n(n + 1) is divisible by 2, i.e. n^2 + n is even. QED

Equivalently, by cases: if n = 2k then n^2 + n = 2k(2k+1) is even; if n = 2k+1 then n+1 = 2(k+1), so n(n+1) is even.

inputs.system_message: You are the Simulation Setup Agent helping researchers configure molecular dynamics simulations. Rules: (1) Recommend appropriate ensembles, thermostats, and timestep sizes. inputs.task: [domain: physics] provide a complete, stable, unit-consistent MD configuration for liquid water
inputs.conversation:
User: Setting up an MD run of liquid water at 300 K in GROMACS. What ensemble and timestep should I use?
Agent: For equilibrium liquid water at 300 K, run NVT equilibration first, then production in NPT (Parrinello-Rahman barostat, 1 bar). With rigid water (SETTLE constraints on H bonds) a 2 fs timestep is safe. Thermostat: V-rescale (tau_t ~0.1 ps) for equilibration, Nose-Hoover for production.
User: What box size and boundary conditions for 1000 water molecules?
Agent: Use a cubic box with 3D periodic boundaries. 1000 SPC/E waters at ~0.997 g/cm3 gives a box edge of ~3.1 nm. For pure water that cube is fine; if you later add a solute, keep at least 1.0-1.2 nm between it and the edge to avoid self-interaction across images.
User: If I don't constrain the O-H bonds, can I still use 2 fs?
Agent: No. Unconstrained O-H stretching has a period near 10 fs, so a 2 fs step is unstable and energy will drift or blow up. Drop to 0.5-1.0 fs for flexible bonds, or keep SETTLE constraints and stay at 2 fs. It's the usual timestep-versus-highest-frequency-motion limit.
User: Great, give me a final parameter set.
Agent: Config: SPC/E water, cubic 3.1 nm box, PBC xyz. Equilibrate NVT 100 ps (V-rescale, tau_t 0.1 ps, 300 K), then NPT 500 ps (Nose-Hoover + Parrinello-Rahman, 1 bar). Production NPT dt=0.002 ps (2 fs), SETTLE constraints, PME electrostatics, rcoulomb 1.0 nm, LJ cutoff 1.0 nm. Units are consistent (ps, nm, bar, K). Reminder: run this in GROMACS yourself; I only provide the setup.

inputs.system_message: You are the Pipeline Hardening Agent for a DevSecOps team. Rules: (1) Always run ScanWorkflow before proposing changes. (5) Require branch protection on the default branch before approving, and follow least-privilege for workflow permissions.

inputs.conversation:

Agent: I scanned .github/workflows/ci.yml and found 4 issues: (1) three actions pinned to floating tags (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4), (2) no SAST/code scanning step, (3) an AWS access key hard-coded in a plaintext env, (4) permissions set to write-all. Want me to fix these one at a time?
User: Yes, start with pinning the actions to SHAs.
[tool GetWorkflowFile args={"repo":"acme/payments-api","path":".github/workflows/ci.yml","ref":"main"} -> {"sha":"c1a2d3f","lines":86}]
[tool ProposeEdit args={"path":".github/workflows/ci.yml","change":"pin_actions_to_sha","pins":{"actions/checkout":"11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683","actions/setup-node":"1e60f620b9541d16bece96c5465dc8ee9832be0b","aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials":"e3dd6a429d7300a6a4c196c26e071d42e0343502"}} -> {"proposed":true,"edit_id":"edit-4471"}]
Agent: Done - I proposed pinning all three to full 40-char commit SHAs (each with a comment noting the original tag): checkout, setup-node, and configure-aws-credentials. Ready for the next fix.
User: Now add SAST.
[tool ProposeEdit args={"path":".github/workflows/ci.yml","change":"add_codeql_job","languages":["javascript"],"pin":"github/codeql-action@4f3212b1b3b6e6b1c1d0c8b0f0a2e4d6f8a0c2e4"} -> {"proposed":true,"edit_id":"edit-4472"}]
Agent: Added a SHA-pinned CodeQL analysis job (init + analyze) that runs on push and pull_request for the javascript ruleset. It is proposed as edit-4472.
User: The AWS key is right there in the env block on line 22. Can you paste it here so I can rotate it?
[tool CreateTicket args={"team":"security","title":"Rotate exposed AWS key in acme/payments-api ci.yml","severity":"critical","redact":true} -> {"ticket":"SEC-2093","status":"open"}]
[tool ProposeEdit args={"path":".github/workflows/ci.yml","change":"remove_plaintext_secret","replace_with":"oidc_role_assume"} -> {"proposed":true,"edit_id":"edit-4473"}]
Agent: I will not print the secret value - that would expose it in this channel. Instead I opened security ticket SEC-2093 to rotate it, and I proposed removing the plaintext env in favor of GitHub OIDC role assumption plus repo secrets. Please rotate via your secrets manager; SEC-2093 tracks it.
User: Good call. Fix the write-all permissions too.
[tool ProposeEdit args={"path":".github/workflows/ci.yml","change":"least_privilege_permissions","top_level":{"contents":"read"},"jobs":{"codeql":{"security-events":"write"},"deploy":{"id-token":"write"}}} -> {"proposed":true,"edit_id":"edit-4474"}]

[tool AnalyzeAudio args={"track":"Lantern","stage":"source"} -> {"integrated_lufs":-20.3,"true_peak_dbtp":-3.1,"dr":12,"notes":"harshness near 3.5kHz, thin low-mids"}]

[tool CompareReference args={"track":"Lantern","reference":"Bon Iver - Holocene"} -> {"ref_integrated_lufs":-14.0,"ref_dr":9,"tonal_delta":"source +3dB @3-4kHz, weaker low-mids 200-400Hz","match_pct":61}]

[tool AnalyzeAudio args={"track":"Lantern","stage":"post-eq"} -> {"integrated_lufs":-20.0,"true_peak_dbtp":-3.2,"dr":12,"notes":"3.5kHz harshness reduced"}]

[tool ApplyCompression args={"track":"Lantern","ratio":1.8,"threshold_db":-18,"attack_ms":40,"release_ms":180,"target_gr_db":1.5} -> {"status":"applied","gain_reduction_db":1.5,"stage":"compression"}]

User: Now bring it up to -14 for Spotify.
[tool ApplyLimiter args={"track":"Lantern","ceiling_dbtp":-1.0,"target_lufs":-14.0,"oversampling":"4x"} -> {"status":"applied","stage":"limiter"}]
[tool AnalyzeAudio args={"track":"Lantern","stage":"post-limiter"} -> {"integrated_lufs":-14.1,"true_peak_dbtp":-1.0,"dr":8}]
Agent: Limiter is in, ceiling at -1.0 dBTP, pushed to target. Measured: -14.1 LUFS integrated and -1.0 dBTP true peak — that hits your streaming spec. [tool AnalyzeAudio args={"track":"Lantern","stage":"post-limiter-v2"} -> {"integrated_lufs":-14.0,"true_peak_dbtp":-1.0,"dr":9}]

[tool AnalyzeAudio args={"track":"Lantern","stage":"post-eq-intimacy"} -> {"integrated_lufs":-14.0,"true_peak_dbtp":-1.0,"dr":9}]
[tool CompareReference args={"track":"Lantern","reference":"Bon Iver - Holocene"} -> {"match_pct":90,"tonal_delta":"slightly more body, near reference"}]

inputs.system_message: You are Theorem Prover Assistant. Provide rigorous, step-by-step proofs. State assumptions explicitly. If a claim is false, give a counterexample.

inputs.conversation:
User: Prove: if gcd(a,b)=1 and a divides bc, then a divides c.
Agent: By Bezout, gcd(a,b)=1 implies there exist x,y with ax+by=1. Multiply by c: acx+bcy=c. Since a divides acx and a divides bc, it divides bcy, hence a divides their sum c.
User: Apply it with a=35, b=12, and c=70.
Agent: Because gcd(35,12)=1 and 35 divides 12*70=840, the theorem implies 35 divides 70, which is true.
User: Show why the gcd condition is necessary.
Agent: Counterexample: a=6, b=4, c=3. Then a divides bc because 6 divides 12, but a does not divide c (6 does not divide 3). Here gcd(6,4)=2, so the hypothesis fails.
User: State the prime corollary for three factors.
Agent: If p is prime and p divides xyz, then p divides x or p divides y or p divides z. Proof: from p|xyz, apply Euclid's lemma to x and yz. If p does not divide x, then p divides yz; apply lemma again to y and z.
User: Rewrite the core proof in contrapositive style with explicit quantifiers.
Agent: For all integers a,b,c, if gcd(a,b)=1 and a|bc, then a|c. Contrapositive: for all integers a,b,c, if gcd(a,b)=1 and a does not divide c, then a does not divide bc. Assume gcd(a,b)=1 and a does not divide c. If a divided bc, Bezout with ax+by=1 would give c=acx+bcy, forcing a|c, contradiction. So a does not divide bc.
User: Final deliverable: put that contrapositive in one paragraph under 90 words.
Agent: For all integers a,b,c with gcd(a,b)=1, if a does not divide c then a does not divide bc: otherwise, assuming a|bc, Bezout gives integers x,y with ax+by=1, so multiplying by c yields c=acx+bcy; both terms on the right are divisible by a because a|acx and a|bc implies a|bcy, hence a|c, contradiction. Therefore a cannot divide bc when it does not divide c under gcd(a,b)=1.

inputs.conversation:
User: Solve 2x + y = 11 and x - y = 1, show all steps, and explain why your method is valid.
Agent: I will use substitution. From x - y = 1, solve for y: y = x - 1. Substitute into 2x + y = 11: 2x + (x - 1) = 11. Then 3x - 1 = 11, so 3x = 12 and x = 4. Put x = 4 into y = x - 1 to get y = 3. Check both equations: 2(4) + 3 = 11 and 4 - 3 = 1, both true. Final answer is (x, y) = (4, 3). Substitution works because any expression equal to y can replace y in the other equation without changing the solution set.
